quizzes.title: Farm Safeguards and CBAM
quizzes.passage:
Agriculture is a sensitive area in the India-EU agreement. Under the agreement, duties on over 90% of bilateral trade have been removed, while sensitive items are handled separately. To protect rural livelihoods and domestic food security, both India and the European Union have maintained comprehensive negative lists for sensitive commodities. Products on these lists remain outside the tariff reduction framework, and the lists are meant to shield small-scale farmers from import surges.

Protection also extends to names and origins. A parallel agreement reinforces legal protection for geographical indications, preventing unauthorised use or imitation of iconic products in either market. Such a parallel agreement sits alongside the main trade terms.

Environmental rules form another strand. The European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism is an EU policy that imposes a carbon price on imports of selected goods from countries with less stringent climate regulations. India has viewed this measure as a possible form of green protectionism that could undermine export competitiveness. To support the transition, the European Union has promised financial and technical help for Indian industries seeking decarbonisation, and a Technical Cooperation Group will help exporters verify carbon footprints.

The agreement's safeguards therefore cover both agriculture and the environment. Together, these safeguards show how the agreement pairs market opening with protection for vulnerable sectors.

questions.q: Which of the following items is excluded from India's tariff reduction framework?
questions.explanation: Poultry is one of India's four excluded items, along with dairy, wheat and rice.

questions.q: Which of the following is excluded from the European Union's tariff reduction framework?
questions.explanation: The EU's negative list covers beef, sugar and rice, while dairy and wheat are on India's list.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT among the sectors covered by the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism?
questions.explanation: CBAM covers cement, aluminium, fertilisers, iron and steel, hydrogen and electricity, while textiles instead gain zero-duty access to the EU.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Importers under the CBAM must buy certificates that correspond to the embedded carbon emissions in their goods.
Reason (R): The price of these certificates is linked to the carbon price of the EU Emissions Trading System.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are in the booklet, but the ETS-linked price explains how certificates are priced rather than why importers must buy them.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Transitional phase (2023-2025)   ->   A. Allowed if the carbon tax was paid in the exporting country
II. Dairy   ->   B. Mandatory emissions reporting with no financial levy
III. Credit for a carbon tax already paid   ->   C. Excluded from the EU's tariff reduction framework
IV. Sugar   ->   D. Excluded from India's tariff reduction framework
questions.explanation: Each correct pairing follows the booklet's CBAM timeline, credit rule and negative lists.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. India received a most-favoured-nation assurance under CBAM.
II. India received a full exemption from CBAM.
III. Wheat is excluded from India's tariff reduction framework.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: India got an MFN assurance but not a full exemption, and wheat is on India's negative list.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Iron and steel is a sector covered by CBAM.
II. Rice is excluded from India's tariff reduction framework.
III. Beef is excluded from India's tariff reduction framework.
questions.explanation: Iron and steel and rice are correct, while beef is on the EU's list rather than India's.

quizzes.title: Negative Lists and Carbon Rules
quizzes.passage:
Negative lists are a feature of the India-EU agreement. Each side has listed sensitive farm goods that stay outside its tariff cuts, so that livelihoods and food security are protected. The lists are intended to keep small-scale farmers from sudden import surges.

Geographical indications also receive attention. A parallel agreement helps stop unauthorised use or imitation of iconic products in both markets.

The European Union's carbon border measure applies to selected imports, and importers must buy certificates tied to the emissions embedded in their goods. An earlier phase required only reporting, without any payment. India has been given an assurance on its treatment under the measure, and a cooperation group will help verify carbon footprints. Indian industries are also receiving European support for decarbonisation.

The mechanism is part of a wider climate package in the EU, aligned with its net-zero targets. It seeks to prevent carbon leakage, meaning companies relocating production to countries with weaker emission norms. Among its objectives is a level playing field, so that imported goods face a carbon cost comparable to EU-made products. Indian exporters also face stringent EU requirements for pesticide residues, certification and labelling. Data governance differences between the EU and India have also been noted.

questions.q: Which grain appears on the negative lists of both India and the European Union?
questions.explanation: Rice is excluded by both sides, while the EU list also includes beef and sugar.

questions.q: How much, in EUR million, has the EU pledged to help Indian industries decarbonise?
questions.explanation: The booklet records a pledge of EUR 500 million for decarbonisation of Indian industries.

questions.q: Which years made up the earlier phase in which CBAM required only emissions reporting? (format: YYYY-YYYY)
questions.explanation: The transitional phase ran from 2023 to 2025 and involved reporting only.

questions.q: Name the CBAM-covered sector listed immediately after cement.
questions.explanation: The booklet lists cement, aluminium, fertilisers, iron and steel, hydrogen and electricity in that order.

questions.q: What acronym names the carbon market whose price the CBAM certificate price follows?
questions.explanation: CBAM certificate prices are linked to the EU ETS carbon price.

questions.q: Name the last sector in the list of CBAM-covered sectors.
questions.explanation: Electricity is the final entry in the booklet's list of six CBAM sectors.

questions.q: Where must a carbon tax have been paid for an importer to receive a credit under CBAM? (two words)
questions.explanation: A credit is allowed if a carbon tax was already paid in the exporting country.

quizzes.title: Towards 2030 Agenda Pillars
quizzes.passage:
India and the European Union have taken their ties beyond trade. Their joint strategic agenda aims to move the relationship from a mainly trade-oriented engagement into a multi-dimensional strategic partnership. It is meant to act as a structured action roadmap for a period marked by geopolitical uncertainty, economic fragmentation and rising protectionism.

The agenda is arranged into several pillars. The economic pillar centres on implementing the free trade agreement, while technology cooperation covers emerging areas and resilient supply chains. Defence cooperation is being reshaped, moving away from a simple buyer-seller relationship. Connectivity projects also feature in the plan. Cyber cooperation includes a partnership between the CBI and Europol. The EU's Global Gateway initiative is among the infrastructure efforts linked to the agenda.

The wider context matters. India is actively reducing its reliance on the US market, and the European market is presented as a stable, rules-based alternative. The agreement is described as reducing dependence on a single market. Space and cyber cooperation is also under way, including collaboration between ISRO and the European Space Agency. Joint research on advanced technologies is another area.

Cooperation on green transition and decarbonisation is also part of the agenda. The agenda builds on ties that have been developing for many years.

questions.q: Under which pillar of the 'Towards 2030' agenda does maritime security in the Indo-Pacific fall?
questions.explanation: The Security and Defence pillar focuses on maritime security in the Indo-Pacific region.

questions.q: Under which pillar does the European Legal Gateway in India fall?
questions.explanation: The Enablers pillar, covering skills and mobility, includes a European Legal Gateway in India.

questions.q: Which pillar includes plans for 6G, semiconductors and quantum computing?
questions.explanation: The Technology and Innovation pillar covers joint development in semiconductors, 6G and quantum computing.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The 'Towards 2030' agenda is a five-year strategic framework.
Reason (R): It was adopted at the 16th India-EU Summit.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are in the booklet, but adoption at a summit does not explain why the framework runs for five years.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Green Hydrogen Task Force   ->   A. Connectivity and Global Challenges pillar
II. Exploratory talks on Horizon Europe   ->   B. Technology and Innovation pillar
III. IMEC acceleration   ->   C. Security and Defence pillar
IV. Joint R&D on drones and sensor systems   ->   D. Prosperity and Sustainability pillar
questions.explanation: Each initiative sits under the pillar the booklet places it in: green hydrogen under Prosperity, Horizon Europe under Technology, IMEC under Connectivity and drones under Security.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Mutual recognition of professional qualifications is targeted by 2030.
II. The Security and Defence pillar focuses on the Arctic region.
III. The Technology and Innovation pillar includes the Trade and Technology Council.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Qualification recognition is targeted by 2030 and the Trade and Technology Council sits under Technology and Innovation, while the security focus is the Indo-Pacific rather than the Arctic.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. IMEC is part of the Connectivity pillar.
II. The agenda was adopted at the 15th India-EU Summit.
III. The Enablers pillar covers skills and mobility.
questions.explanation: IMEC and the Enablers pillar are correctly placed, but the agenda was adopted at the 16th summit, not the 15th.

quizzes.title: Strategic Agenda and US Tariffs
quizzes.passage:
India and the European Union have agreed on a joint strategic agenda that looks beyond trade. Its goal is to change the relationship from a mainly trade-oriented engagement into a broader, multi-dimensional strategic partnership. The agenda is described as a structured roadmap for managing geopolitical uncertainty, economic fragmentation and rising protectionism.

Its initiatives are grouped into pillars. The economic pillar stresses effective implementation of the trade agreement, with the aim of linking India to a very large combined market. Other pillars cover technology cooperation, joint defence work, cross-border connectivity and people-focused measures such as skills and mobility. The plan also refers to joint development of advanced technologies.

The US factor is also important. After tariff measures from Washington hit Indian goods, India is seeking to rely less on the American market. The European market is presented as a stable, rules-based alternative, and the agreement is said to offer a buffer against changes in US trade policy.

Connectivity and infrastructure feature prominently, including a corridor linking India with Europe through the Middle East and the EU's infrastructure financing efforts in India and Africa. Cooperation on space and cyber issues is also part of the plan. The agenda is also linked to the wider partnership between India and the EU, which has deepened over the years.

questions.q: What target year appears in the official title of the India-EU joint strategic agenda?
questions.explanation: The official title is 'Towards 2030: Joint India-EU Comprehensive Strategic Agenda'.

questions.q: What is the acronym of the India-Middle East-Europe corridor that the agenda seeks to fast-track?
questions.explanation: IMEC is the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor, which the agenda seeks to fast-track.

questions.q: What is the value, in EUR billion, of the EU's Global Gateway Initiative?
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the Global Gateway Initiative a value of EUR 300 billion.

questions.q: What is the name of the European mechanism to be set up in India to streamline lawful migration for skilled professionals?
questions.explanation: The agenda's enablers pillar provides for a European Legal Gateway in India.

questions.q: What percentage of reciprocal tariffs did the US impose on Indian goods in August 2025? (in per cent)
questions.explanation: The booklet records 50% reciprocal tariffs on Indian goods imposed in August 2025.

questions.q: Which single word completes the phrase describing India and the EU's joint position in global trade: the '___ Pole'?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes India and the EU jointly creating a 'Third Pole' in global trade.

questions.q: What US trade surplus figure, in USD billion, is described as exposed to potential sanctions?
questions.explanation: India's US-market surplus of USD 45.8 billion is described as exposed to potential sanctions.

quizzes.title: EU Institutions and Ties
quizzes.passage:
The European Union is a political and economic union of 27 member states, with a set of shared institutions. Its roots lie in a cooperation arrangement among a small group of countries, and it has since grown into one of the world's largest economic blocs. Its climate ambition is to cut net greenhouse emissions by 55 per cent by 2030, compared with 1990 levels. Services make up most of the union's economic output. The union's single market is one of its defining features. Adoption of EU regulations, sometimes called the Brussels Effect, shapes standards for partners beyond Europe. Standards set by the union can influence exporters in other markets. Summits between the two sides began in 2000.

Several bodies share responsibilities within the union. Each has a distinct role in the union's work. The union also has a court that deals with questions about EU law.

Member states differ widely in population and geography, and the union's membership has changed over time. The United Kingdom's departure reduced the number of members, although the union remains an important partner for India.

India and the EU have maintained diplomatic relations for a long time, and their ties have grown into a strategic partnership supported by trade, investment and institutional dialogue.

questions.q: Which EU institution proposes laws, enforces rules and manages the budget?
questions.explanation: The European Commission is the executive body that proposes laws, enforces rules and manages the budget.

questions.q: In which year did the United Kingdom withdraw from the EU (Brexit)?
questions.explanation: The UK's withdrawal in 2020 reduced EU membership from 28 to 27.

questions.q: Which EU member state is the largest by area?
questions.explanation: The booklet says France is the largest by area, while Germany has the largest population.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The euro was launched in 1999.
Reason (R): The euro is the currency of the euro area, which is formed by the member states that use it.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are in the booklet, but the currency's status does not explain the launch year.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. European Council   ->   A. Ensures uniform application of EU law
II. Court of Justice of the EU   ->   B. Manages the euro and monetary policy for the eurozone
III. European Central Bank   ->   C. Co-legislates and approves the budget
IV. European Parliament   ->   D. Sets the overall political direction of the EU
questions.explanation: The booklet's key institutions section assigns each body its function: Council sets direction, the Court ensures uniformity, the ECB manages the euro and Parliament co-legislates.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to the EU in 2012.
II. Malta is the EU's largest member by population.
III. The European Council is made up of heads of state or government.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The EU received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2012 and the European Council is composed of heads of state or government, whereas Malta is the smallest member.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Members of the European Parliament are elected every five years.
II. Ireland is part of the Schengen Area.
III. All EU members except Cyprus and Ireland are in the Schengen Area.
questions.explanation: Parliament elections are held every five years and Ireland is one of the two EU exceptions to Schengen membership, so only the second statement is wrong.

quizzes.title: EU Origins and India Ties
quizzes.passage:
The European Union began as a cooperation arrangement among a small group of countries and has since grown to 27 member states. It now operates through a set of institutions that together propose, decide and enforce EU policy.

India's association with the bloc is long-standing. Diplomatic ties were built with a predecessor of the present union, and relations were later raised to a strategic footing. The EU is one of India's major trade and investment partners. Summits between the two sides began in 2000. Leaders have met at summits since then.

Member states differ in size and population, and the union's membership has changed over time. The union's common border-free zone and its shared currency are both well-known features of European integration. Adoption of EU regulations, sometimes called the Brussels Effect, shapes standards for partners beyond Europe. Standards set by the union can influence exporters in other markets.

Institutional dialogue has also deepened. Its common currency is used across much of the union. India and the EU have set up several mechanisms, including a trade and technology body and a connectivity initiative linking India with Europe through the Middle East. Its climate ambition is to cut net greenhouse emissions by 55 per cent by 2030, compared with 1990 levels.

questions.q: In which year did India establish diplomatic relations with the European Economic Community, the EU's predecessor?
questions.explanation: India established diplomatic relations with the European Economic Community in 1962.

questions.q: In which city was the first India-EU Summit held, in 2000?
questions.explanation: The booklet records the first India-EU Summit in 2000 as held in Lisbon.

questions.q: What was India's export value to the EU in 2024-25, in USD billion?
questions.explanation: India's exports to the EU were USD 75.85 billion in 2024-25, against imports of USD 60.68 billion.

questions.q: Since which year has the Schengen Area allowed border-free travel, according to the booklet? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Schengen Area has allowed border-free travel since 1985.

questions.q: Which EU member state has the largest population?
questions.explanation: The booklet names Germany as the EU member with the largest population.

questions.q: In which year was the India-EU Trade and Technology Council established?
questions.explanation: The booklet dates the India-EU Trade and Technology Council to 2023.

questions.q: What is the acronym of the 1951 community of six countries that was the EU's forerunner?
questions.explanation: The EU began as the European Coal and Steel Community, formed in 1951 by six founding members.
